title: docs(plugin-detail): the reference-rail README says `entries` go in the `properties` bag, and that the validator refuses a flat one (objectui#10872)
body:
Fixes #10872
Clause-②: no

This is the card's last item: the `record:reference_rail` sentence in the `@object-ui/plugin-detail` README (site `5943728376`), corrected under ruling A (the `properties` bag is the contract). The earlier items of the card landed in objectui#11570 (merged as `8d0ca91`).

## What changes

One file, `packages/plugin-detail/README.md`, the paragraph after the "Adding the rail to a custom `Page`" example.

Before:

> The renderer reads `entries` from both `schema.entries` and `schema.properties.entries` so either spec-style or flat authoring works.

After:

> The `entries` go in the node's `properties` bag, as the example shows: that bag is the contract, and `objectui validate` refuses a flat `entries` written on the node itself, naming `properties.entries`.

The corrected paragraph teaches no flat spelling as working and carries no "flat still renders" aside, as the ruling and the precedent (objectui#11566 for objectui#11550, decision A) require.

## Premise check, measured on `main` at `f1c9379`

A throwaway probe (deleted before the commit; nothing of it is in the diff) ran both faces over the flat node and the bag node:

| face | `{ type: 'record:reference_rail', entries: [...] }` (flat) | `{ type: 'record:reference_rail', properties: { entries: [...] } }` |
|:--|:--|:--|
| `safeValidateSchema` (what `objectui validate` runs) | `success=false`, `invalid_type` at `['entries']` | `success=true` |
| `StrictAnyComponentSchema` | `success=false`, `invalid_type` at `['entries']` | `success=true` |

Both faces answer the flat node with the same issue message, quoted from the run: "Unrecognized key(s) on this `record:reference_rail` node: `entries`. Did you mean `entries` → `properties.entries`? A `record:reference_rail` node takes its props in its `properties` bag, where `@objectstack/spec`'s `ComponentPropsMap['record:reference_rail']` row declares them: write `{ "type": "record:reference_rail", "properties": { "entries": … } }` (objectui#10872)." So the README sentence taught a spelling that the validator refuses. The premise is live on current `main`.

## Sweep of the same README (this file only)

I read every `record:*` mention and every code block in `packages/plugin-detail/README.md`, and searched it for flat-teaching words (`flat`, `tolerat`, `either`, `alias`, `spec-style`, `also works`).

- The `record:reference_rail` paragraph above is the only line that taught a flat member as working. Changed.
- The `record:activity` tab example puts `limit` and `showCompleted` under `properties`, and its prose says the inputs go in the `properties` bag. Unchanged.
- The `record:related_list` example was already moved under `properties` by objectui#11512. Its prose sentences about "the node's `filter`", `sort` and `columns` name spec props and do not teach a flat spelling. Unchanged.
- The opt-in and opt-out sections are `buildDefaultPageSchema` options, not node keys. Unchanged.

Mechanical check that nothing else moved: the README's 10 fenced blocks are byte-identical before and after, and so are its headings and link lines.

## Changeset

No changeset, derived from the gate and not guessed. `scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs` counts a package's published source as `src/` files, the `index.html` entry, and `files[]` entries, minus `*.md` and `LICENSE*`. A README is a `*.md`, so a README-only change is outside the rule. The gate's own verdict line at `17ed7dc` is in the table below. AGENTS.md states the same exemption in its changeset paragraph. No `skip-changeset` label is applied: that label is not objectui's mechanism.

## Gates, run at `17ed7dc` (the final commit)

Families derived from objectui's own `package.json` and `.github/workflows/` for the path actually changed (`packages/plugin-detail/README.md`).

| command | exit | verdict line |
|:--|:--|:--|
| `pnpm check:control-bytes` | 0 | `check-control-bytes: OK (scanned 10205 tracked text file(s); skipped 85 binary).` |
| `pnpm check:new-line-citations` | 0 | `VERDICT new-cross-file-line-citations: 0 new citation(s), enforcement report-only -> exit 0` |
| `pnpm check:changeset-claims` | 0 | report-only; it lists two pending changesets that name this README. I read both paragraphs: one is about the retired `related` array, the other about the `filter` arity text. Neither says anything about `reference_rail` `entries`, so neither is falsified. |
| `pnpm check:pending-changeset-literals` | 0 | `No test source names a pending changeset.` |
| `pnpm check:doc-types` | 0 | `Every documented component type is registered.` |
| `pnpm check:doc-fences` | 0 | `every TypeScript block in 227 document(s) is fenced ts/tsx/typescript` |
| `pnpm check:doc-example-ids` | 0 | `415 real reference(s) all resolve in the catalog registry.` |
| `pnpm docs:check-links` | 0 | `Links are valid across 17 scan roots.` |
| `node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs` | 0 | `No source or published contract of a released package changed in this range, so no changeset is owed.` |

NOT MEASURED: `pnpm check:readme-exports`, `pnpm check:doc-snippets`, `pnpm check:doc-examples`. Reason: all three need `dist/` builds (the gate prints `its type entry ... is not on disk -- run pnpm build first`, and a scoped build of the packages the covered documents import), and this worktree is unbuilt. This is a missing prerequisite, so the exit codes (1, 2, 2) are not verdicts on the diff. They judge fenced code and its imports; the 10 fenced blocks of this README are byte-identical to `f1c9379`, so the diff gives them nothing new to judge. CI builds and runs them.

Lint and the test suites are not owed for a prose-only diff and were not run.

## Acceptance notes

- The runtime renderers still read the flat spelling as well: `record-reference-rail.tsx` reads `schema.entries` before `schema.properties.entries`, and its docblock says "The rail accepts a node either flattened ... or enveloped". `record-history.tsx` has the same two-way read. The card scopes the fix to the README sentence ("The runtime does read both spellings, so the fix is the README sentence only"), so neither file is touched here. Noted, not filed: a renderer-side tolerance that sits outside this card's scope; what the README now teaches is the validator's contract.
- No other markdown file in the tree names `record:reference_rail` as a flat-authored block (searched `*.md` and `*.mdx`; the hits are changesets and the README itself).
- A sibling dev runs objectui#11581 (`packages/app-shell/src/views/`). No file overlap.
